inline_text:
## Summary

Three fixes to chapter identity, all found while running the sync pipeline end to end and driving it to zero drift.

## Changesets

**`fix(sync-chapters)`: grant Drive access to an address Drive can actually honour**

An accepted organizer whose intake address has no Google account behind it could not be granted at all — Drive refuses such a permission unless it may email an invitation, so the grant was skipped and the lock phase aborted on the ungranted organizer. `Drive Email` already recorded the address on the ACL but nothing read it. It now drives the grant, while the intake `Email` is never rewritten.

Three guards, because that cell is hand-editable and decides who holds standing write access to a chapter's trackers, budgets and CRM:
- the authority stays on the intake row — the column moves *where* a grant lands, never manufactures one, and `assert_all_accepted` re-derives the recorded address from its own fresh read
- only a real override counts — blank, the `(no grant)` sentinel, free text, two addresses in one cell, or a restatement of the intake address are all ignored
- two rows disagreeing about one person drop the override entirely, loudly

`track_drive_email` stops overwriting a recorded-but-not-yet-granted address with `(no grant)`.

**`feat(sync-chapters)`: write a new chapter row without waiting for its Luma page**

The Luma gate becomes opt-in (`--require-luma`). A new row is not site-ready until its editorial columns are filled by hand, so holding it never kept a dead CTA off the site — it only delayed the row. The visibility the gate did provide is replaced by `--audit-luma`, which checks **every** feed row's `Chapter Luma Link`, not just today's additions, and exits 2 when one 404s.

**`feat(create-chapter)`: rename an existing chapter everywhere its old name is written**

The capital-city migration renamed three chapters on the Chapters List and stopped there — their Drive folders, CRM workbooks, About docs and design assets kept the old name, and the folder name is what the sync engines match on. `rename_chapter.py` applies the clone-time transform between two arbitrary cities, in place, across four surfaces.

The Luma slug is deliberately **not** renamed unless asked: a chapter's name and its Luma page are two identities, and two of the three affected chapters still have live pages at their old slugs. For the same reason the name pass is kept out of `aaif-<slug>` tokens — an uppercase city name is a substring of its own slug, which silently broke a live link until a test caught it.

## Test Plan

- 28 new checks in `test_rename_chapter.py`; extended `test_sync_access.py`, `test_track_drive_email.py`, `test_sync_chapters.py`
- every skill suite in `aaif-sync-chapters` and `aaif-create-chapter` passes
- `pre-commit run --all-files` green, including the PII and secret-arg guards
- exercised live: the access change granted a real organizer whose address Drive had refused; the rename ran over four chapters with per-file verification re-read from Drive; the pipeline reports `everything in sync` across all five engines
